question: How dependent is Apple on China, and what happened to its sales there?

answer.summary: Apple's dependence on China is material but secondary to the U.S.: Greater China generated $72.56B, or 18.9% of FY2023 net sales [F00850][F00880], and the U.S. and China were the only countries accounting for more than 10% of net sales in FY2023, FY2022 and FY2021 [T00600]. China sales fell 2.2% year-over-year, from $74.20B in FY2022 [F00851][F00881] to $72.56B in FY2023, a -$1.64B change equal to 15% of the company's total -$11.04B (-2.8%) revenue decline [F00014]. In the business-segment view, Americas was the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE at -$7.10B (-4.2%), 64% of the total change [F00838][F00839]; in the geographical view the U.S. led with -$9.29B (-6.3%), 84% of the change [F00877]. By product, Mac was the largest contributor (-$10.82B, -26.9%, 98% of the change) [F00282] and iPhone also declined (-$4.91B, -2.4%, 44%) [F00279], while Services grew +$7.07B (+9.1%), offsetting 64% of the decline [F00010]. Management states that foreign currency weakness relative to the U.S. dollar accounted for more than the entire year-over-year decrease in total net sales [T00275].

drivers: Americas was the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE in the StatementBusinessSegments view: -$7.10B (-4.2%), 64% of the total -$11.04B change [F00838][F00839]; Japan followed at -$1.72B (-6.6%, 16%) [F00856], Greater China at -$1.64B (-2.2%, 15%) [F00850], Europe at -$824.00M (-0.9%, 7%) [F00844], and Rest of Asia Pacific grew +$240.00M (+0.8%), moving AGAINST the total change (offsets 2%) [F00862].

In the StatementGeographical view, the U.S. was the largest contributor at -$9.29B (-6.3%), 84% of the total change [F00877]; China (CN) contributed -$1.64B (-2.2%), 15% [F00880]; Other Countries -$116.00M (-0.1%), 1% [F00883]. Note: Americas (segment, $162.56B) is a broader cut than the U.S. (geographical, $138.57B).

By product, Mac drove the decline (-$10.82B, -26.9%, 98% of the total change) [F00282], with iPhone (-$4.91B, -2.4%, 44%) [F00279], Wearables/Home/Accessories (-$1.40B, -3.4%, 13%) [F00288] and iPad (-$992.00M, -3.4%, 9%) [F00285] also down; Services rose +$7.07B (+9.1%), offsetting 64% of the total change [F00010].

Management attributes more than the entire year-over-year decrease in total net sales to foreign currency weakness, with the decline consisting primarily of lower Mac and iPhone sales partially offset by higher Services [T00275].
risks_and_red_flags: Apple has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of total net sales, and a majority of its supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S., so operations depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions [T00118].

Primary exposure to foreign exchange rate movements relates to non-U.S. dollar-denominated sales, cost of sales and operating expenses worldwide; gross margins on products in foreign countries and on products with foreign-sourced components have been and could be materially adversely affected by FX fluctuations [T00221].
Greater China's 18.9% revenue share [F00850] leaves a meaningful portion of the top line exposed to China-specific conditions, though the U.S. remains the largest market at 36.2% [F00877].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 Greater China revenue of $72.56B declined 2.2% YoY (-$1.64B), contributing 15% of the company-wide -$11.04B (-2.8%) decline, amid Mac/iPhone weakness and FX headwinds [F00850][F00014][T00275]; Americas was the largest segment contributor to the decline at 64% of the change [F00838].
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: Not in the retrieved evidence; no management guidance figures were provided in the 10-K evidence.

follow_up_checks: Verify whether the China decline was concentrated in specific products (iPhone vs. Mac vs. Services) within Greater China, since company-wide Mac weakness drove most of the total decline [F00282].
Quantify the FX impact specifically on Greater China sales versus the company-wide FX effect described in MD&A [T00275].
Assess supply chain concentration risk, given a majority of manufacturing and assembly sites are outside the U.S. [T00118].
Check subsequent quarters or FY2024 data for whether China revenue stabilized or continued to decline after the FY2023 -2.2% [F00850].
Confirm whether long-lived assets in China (referenced in the geographic disclosure [T00600]) indicate significant fixed-asset exposure in the region.
